subject: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finly.com>, Priya Singh <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today, Alex & Priya — good conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the success criteria you called out, and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please reply with any corrections.

High-level pain points we heard
- Interactive streaming UX feels sluggish at peak: users see chunked updates and occasional stalls.
- p95 tail spikes during bursts / background jobs (QA runs) causing timeouts in the frontend.
- Concurrency limits on your current cluster force backs off or queuing; scaling is brittle during sustained peak.

Current stack (as described)
- Self-hosted model serving on GCP, Triton + custom batching layer; 4xA100 nodes today.
- Model: "finly-llm-v1" (FP16), typical response length ~120 tokens, some 1k+ token outliers for reports.
- Traffic pattern: normal day 20–40 concurrent streaming sessions; peaks up to ~180 concurrent users; projected Q4 peak ~250 concurrent.

Success criteria you gave
- End-to-end p95 (interactive streaming UX) <= 400 ms for common queries (avg ~120 tokens).
- Tail p95 (outliers) < 600 ms, and no perceptible stalls during streaming.
- Support 150–200 concurrent interactive streaming sessions with smooth token emission.
- Predictable autoscaling behavior and cost estimate that maps to committed throughput.

Open questions we captured
- Are the 1k+ token reports latency-sensitive in the same way as short chat responses?
- Do you have sample request traces or one week of production logs we can use for a qualification run?
- Any network topology / VPC peering constraints we should know about?

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood runs a short qualification run against a representative sample workload to produce baseline p95 numbers and an initial sizing recommendation (we'll use a copy of your traces / synthetic workload if you provide one).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Aditya) to verify KV cache affinity, batching windows, and streaming chunk size strategy.
3) We'll share a short slide deck with preliminary sizing and assumptions (attached).
4) Tentative timeline: qualification run in 3 business days after we receive traces + topology; deep-dive within the week.

Attachments: finly_p95_latency_slide.pdf (initial sizing & assumptions)

If that all looks right, can we get the sample traces and a network diagram? Also, what days/times next week work for a 60-minute deep technical call? I'm blocking out Thu/Fri mornings PST for now.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and captures everything I had in mind. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 1k+ token reports are generally less latency-sensitive; they run as background jobs for exports. The interactive chat paths are our primary UX concern.
- We can pull a week of production traces and a subset of traffic (redacted) for you. We'll also export 24 hours of streaming traces with client-side timings.
- Network: we have GCP VPC with restricted egress, but can set up VPC peering / private connectivity for qualification if needed. I'll attach a basic topology diagram in my follow-up.

Would love to get an estimate for how long the qualification run takes and any specific artifact formats you prefer (e.g., JSON traces, CSV histograms). We can do Thu 10:00–11:00 AM PST for the tech deep-dive.

Appreciate it —
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | Finly
alex@finly.com | 617-555-0124

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@finly.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Thanks Alex — Marissa, thanks for the recap. A few technical clarifications and what we'll do on our side for the qualification run: 

Questions / clarifications:
- Avg response length: you said ~120 tokens typically. Can you provide the token distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99) or just a sample of 500 requests? That helps set batching windows.
- Do you rely on single-request KV cache affinity (session stickiness) for user conversations, or can we treat requests as independent for initial sizing?
- Are you using any non-standard tokenization or custom tokenizer that changes token counts vs. huggingface defaults?
- Client-side timing: for streaming UX we want both server-side per-token timestamps and client-side emission timings if possible.
- Rate limits: do you have global or per-user rate limits we should respect during the qualification run?

What we'll run:
- Synthetic replay of your sample traces on a Redwood test pool with an identical model binary (if you can provide) or a compatible open quantized variant.
- We'll measure end-to-end p50/p90/p95/p99 for both single-request and streaming (per-chunk) emission.
- We'll include a concurrency sweep (50, 100, 150, 200, 250) to map tail behavior and identify breakpoints.

Deliverables (after qualification):
- Perf baseline report (CSV + short deck) with recommended instance types / sizing and an estimated cost curve for hosted/dedicated options.
- A short list of tuning knobs (batching window, max-batch-size, KV cache TTL, streaming chunk size) likely to improve the streaming UX.

Attachment request: please send the topology diagram and a redacted sample of traces (JSON or CSV) — we'll start the replay as soon as we have them.

I'll be on the Thu 10:00 AM PST deep dive. If you want, I can drop a short pre-read (1-2 pages) outlining what we'll measure.

—Aditya
